idea: How to maintain a home water system
title: Preventing Sediment Accumulation in Water Heater Tanks
description: An educational breakdown detailing how mineral sediment settles at the base of a storage water heater and why periodic flushing through the lower drain valve maintains energy efficiency and prevents tank failure.
image_prompt: A clean vertical 9:16 professional technical cutaway illustration of the lower section of a residential storage water heater. The interior view exposes the concave steel tank bottom where a granular layer of heavy calcium sediment has accumulated over the base. A brass drain valve is threaded into the lower tank port, with a garden hose attached. Water mixed with mineral sediment particulates flows through a transparent section of the hose into a bucket. Bright neutral studio lighting highlights realistic steel, brass, and copper textures with crisp detail. Vertical composition centered in the middle frame with uncluttered background space at the top and bottom. Photorealistic textures, high technical accuracy, visually clear assembly. No text, no captions, no logos, no watermarks, no brand names.
visual_story: The cutaway visual allows the viewer to see inside the lower section of a closed storage tank, showing where heavy mineral scale sits relative to the heating zone and the drain port. By displaying sediment leaving through a attached hose, the graphic clearly links the invisible problem inside the tank with the simple physical maintenance step used to correct it.

on_image_text.hook: Sediment Trapped at the Bottom of Your Tank?
on_image_text.explanation: Dissolved minerals settle at the lower dome, creating an insulating barrier that reduces heat transfer.
on_image_text.takeaway: Flush 1-2 gallons through the drain valve periodically until water runs clear.
